_note: THE PERMISSION-FREE PATH (parity F12). `dsx.module.contacts.pick` opens the SYSTEM picker: iOS CNContactPickerViewController, Android ACTION_PICK on the contacts provider, web navigator.contacts.select. None of the three triggers an authorization prompt and none needs a manifest grant, because the user hand-picks and the OS returns only what was picked. This corpus pins that fact so a future refactor cannot quietly route `pick` through the store, and pins the two shapes that are easy to get wrong: a dismissal RESOLVES (it is a user decision, not an error) and a platform with no multi-select SAYS SO rather than returning a one-element array. Runners: TS (@despia/kernel contacts-core.ts, contacts-conformance.test.ts), Kotlin (:core ContactsCore, ContactsConformanceTest), Swift (Engine/iOS/ContactsCore.swift, ContactsConformance in the record lane).

permissionSurface._note: action -> the grant it requires before it will run. `none` is the contract, not an implementation detail: an action listed as `none` that starts prompting is a regression, and an action listed as `read`/`write` that stops refusing is a privacy bug.

cases.name: a single pick returns one contact and never prompts
a dismissed picker RESOLVES cancelled and settles no error
multi-select returns every chosen contact where the platform has it
a platform with no multi-select reports multiple:false, never a silent single
an already-denied store does NOT stop the picker: it needs no grant
fields subsets the hydrated shape and drops nothing else in
a browser with no Contact Picker API refuses in type
